title: Distributed Machine Learning at the Edge — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public fog data science knowledge, fact-checked reference. Training and serving ML across fog nodes: federated learning, split learning, and partitioned inference. Distributed ML at the edge keeps data on devices while models learn collectively. Federated learning trains locally on fog nodes and ships only model updates to an aggregator; split learning cuts the network between device and fog server; partitioned inference places early layers on devices, middle layers on fog nodes, and heavy heads in the cloud. Model compression — quantization, pruning, distillation — makes deep networks fit fog-class hardware. Aggregation must handle non-IID data, stragglers, and dropouts.
